sections.title: Hol? and Hová?
sections.content: *Hol?* asks where someone is, and the place takes *-ban/-ben*. *Hová?* asks where someone is going, and the place takes *-ba/-be*. You can say both in one sentence with *de*: *A boltban vagyok, de a bankba megyek.* (I am in the shop, but I am going to the bank.)

sections.title: Two questions
rows: Where are you? – I am in the shop.
Where are you going? – I am going to the bank.

items.spanish: A boltban vagyok, de a bankba megyek.
items.english: I am in the shop, but I am going to the bank.

items.spanish: Hol van Anna? – A parkban van.
items.english: Where is Anna? – She is in the park.

items.spanish: Hová megy Károly? – A moziba megy.
items.english: Where is Károly going? – He is going to the cinema.
The tourist is in the museum.
Tomorrow I am going to the library.

sections.content: *Hol* goes with *van* or *vagyok*; *hová* goes with *megy*, *mész* or *megyek*.
